{
  "title": "The Keeper’s Ember",
  "world": "Cinematic Storybook Realism",
  "cold_open": "The salt spray bites like a winter frost, whipping against the jagged teeth of the shoreline rocks.",
  "question": "Why does the glass eye of the lighthouse pulse with a rhythmic, amber heartbeat tonight?",
  "journey": "Down in the village, the elders pull their shutters tight against the gale. They speak in hushed tones of the old keeper, a man who vanished into the mist decades ago. But tonight, the rotating beam cuts through the black curtain of the storm. It isn't the flickering, dying gasp of a mechanical failure. It is steady. It is purposeful. It sweeps across the churning foam, tracing the path of ships that haven't sailed these waters in a generation. The gears groan, a heavy, metallic sigh echoing from the tower's hollow bones.",
  "discovery": "A young girl stands at the cliff’s edge, her coat snapping in the wind. She sees the light leap—not a steady beam, but a flare of recognition. In that flash, she sees a silhouette against the pane: a shadow moving with practiced grace, polishing the heavy lens.",
  "emotional_turn": "It isn't a ghost seeking a haunting, but a memory refusing to fade. The light isn't calling for help; it is keeping a promise made to the sea. It is the warmth of a hand on a shoulder, steadying a traveler in the dark.",
  "payoff": "The storm breaks, the wind subsiding into a weary moan. The light stays, soft and constant, refusing to dim even as the clouds part. The keeper is gone, but his vigil remains, a golden thread sewn into the fabric of the night.",
  "after_image": "A single, polished brass key sits on the windowsill, glowing in the dying amber light.",
  "hero_shot": "A massive, soot-stained lens refracting a single beam of gold across a face made of sea-spray and shadow."
}
